topic.title: Metric Learning and Geometric Similarity
topic.overview: A distance function determines which observations a learning system considers similar. This topic learns or designs distances for classification, clustering, adaptation, and comparison of entire datasets. Approaches transform representations, combine multiple distances, or use geometric constructions that emphasize different scales of structure.
topic.whyItMatters: Similarity is task dependent: two examples can be close in raw coordinates yet require different predictions. Learning a metric can improve neighborhood-based decisions, but it can also hide important distinctions if the training objective is too narrow. Dataset-level distances add further questions about scale and high-dimensional behavior.
topic.evolution: Early representatives connect dimensionality reduction and transformation-aware recognition. A 2008 kernel classifier jointly learns its distance embedding and bandwidth, while other work studies class collapse and Bregman geometry. In 2026, magnitude distance introduces a tunable scale for comparing finite datasets and explores its use as a generative training objective.
openQuestions: How can a learned distance remain useful when downstream tasks change?
What evidence shows that dataset similarity corresponds to transferable predictive information?

papers.title: Improved Learning via k-DTW: A Novel Dissimilarity Measure for Curves
papers.tldr: k-DTW offers improved curve-comparison properties and dimension-free learning bounds, with statistical advantages over DTW when k is small relative to curve complexity.

papers.title: MetricEmbedding: Accelerate Metric Nearness by Tropical Inner Product
papers.tldr: MetricEmbedding uses a tropical-inner-product formulation to repair distance matrices efficiently while producing metric-preserving embeddings.

papers.title: Stabilizing Sample Similarity in Representation via Mitigating Random Consistency
papers.tldr: PSED removes a chance-agreement bias from similarity-based representation learning and improves classification results in the reported benchmarks.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Algorithms for Chamfer Distance
papers.tldr: Dynamic Chamfer-distance approximation reduces to approximate nearest-neighbor search, providing provable update-time and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers.title: Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation
papers.tldr: A simpler JMMD formulation unifies adaptation distances and reveals why alignment can reduce class discrimination.

papers.title: Siegel Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper constructs classification layers for Siegel-space neural networks and reports state-of-the-art results on evaluated radar and node-classification datasets.

papers.title: Magnitude Distance: A Geometric Measure of Dataset Similarity
papers.tldr: Magnitude distance compares finite datasets across adjustable geometric scales and provides useful signals for generative-model training.
